reason: E2 directly supports the link between multi-element mixing, lattice distortion, sluggish diffusion, and prevention of phase separation in nanoparticles. E1 supports that local chemical ordering (related to configurational entropy) increases activation barriers, but it does not address nanoparticles or the specific CoCrFeMnNi system. E3 only describes synthesis of the nanoparticles, providing no evidence for the mechanistic premises. The key premise that reducing configurational entropy lowers diffusion barriers and causes earlier segregation is not directly supported by any cited evidence.
premises: High configurational entropy in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles produces significant lattice distortions
These lattice distortions increase atomic diffusion barriers (sluggish diffusion)
Increased diffusion barriers kinetically stabilize the single-phase solid solution against phase separation
Reducing configurational entropy (via slight off-stoichiometry) lowers diffusion barriers
Lowered diffusion barriers cause earlier phase segregation and elemental clustering
